scientific_question: Do mammal species' detected diel-time distributions transport to new sites and later years better when their temporal coordinate is aligned to sunrise/sunset than when learned in clock hours; is residual species-season structure still needed after the solar transform?

source.archive: Mayer et al. Rhode Island wildlife camera trap survey 2018 to 2023, Zenodo version 3
source.source_label_has_changed: Version 3 contains image-level detections, NOT necessarily independent events

source_timezone.solar_reference: NOAA approximate sunrise/sunset at 90.833-degree apparent zenith

design.duplicate_key: site + camera + normalized species + declared season
design.independence_unit: physical site (NOT camera images, photo sequences or site-years)
design.animal_detection_target: six four-hour local civil-clock bins among retained species detections, NOT activity independent of detection bias
design.frozen_solar_target: equinoctial double-anchored 24-hour phase with sunrise at 06 and sunset at 18
design.identical_score_target: six local-clock bins for ALL four models; solar phase histograms pushed forward exactly into clock-hour bin probabilities
design.training_weight: equal within species x physical site x season-year, each retained event weight reciprocal count within that stratum
design.score_name: heldout log probability, with clipped numeric probabilities only after Jeffreys smoothing; no posthoc model selection

models.solar: species sunrise/sunset-anchored six-bin phase distribution mapped to clock-hour six-bin target each event date and site
models.clock_season: species x season clock-hour six-bin distribution
models.solar_season: species x season solar phase six-bin distribution mapped to the same clock-hour target
models.capacity_note: clock and solar share six-bin histogram capacity and identical Jeffreys smoothing; season-conditioned controls are more flexible

registered_hypotheses.primary: solar vs clock held-out log-score difference positive in both season groups at physically heldout sites in future years
registered_hypotheses.solar_specificity_negative_control: using solar curves at date shifted by 183 calendar days must NOT deliver equal or better site-level gain than correct date on both season groups
registered_hypotheses.secondary_residual_season: solar x season improves over solar x species-only if seasonal plasticity persists beyond solar phase
registered_hypotheses.other_model_sensitivity: clock x season vs clock only
registered_hypotheses.interpretation_if_primary_positive: supports solar-phase predictive transport on camera detections, not proof of photoperiod causality
registered_hypotheses.interpretation_if_primary_negative: fixed clock outpredicts this particular phase-alignment model in the studied site/year support, not absence of seasonal response

validation.primary_unit_weight: equal mean per physical heldout site and season, collapsing repeated years before aggregate
validation.uncertainty: resample physical site IDs with 2000 predeclared bootstrap draws, seed 2026100803; report same-draw joint two-season distribution
validation.gate: both winter and summer primary mean gains >0 with 95% one-sided site-bootstrap lower bounds >0; negative control degrades across both seasons; otherwise MIXED/NOT_SUPPORTED/UNAVAILABLE
validation.null_baseline: clock and solar trained only from earlier years and disjoint physical sites
validation.unseen_species: training-only species admission; unseen later-year species are out-of-support, report count but no retraining

claims_not_allowed: day/night ecological activity rate without timestamp-specific camera effort
true solar clock if original camera timestamp zone or DST is unverified
reclassification of closed Snapshot Serengeti, bat, BOP or tawaki terminals
qualified v5 or future-refit p_success based on this new empirical analysis
hard_stops: First inspect source archive bytes and exact member schemas; if alias/schema ambiguity or missing metadata prevent coherent site/date pairing, stop without result
Do not tune folds, training/heldout year boundaries, pseudocounts, time bins or admission thresholds after the first detection-row outcomes
Never treat multiple cameras/photo rows/season-years of same site as independent sites
If photo time zone cannot be verified, report as exploratory rather than mechanistic primary
Current code and source selection are a separate study; none of old prospectively closed endpoints may be re-opened
